The other components and IC1 chip connections are for the normal operation of the demodulator for the frequencies that are used in this experiment.
The demodulator chip is set up to operate using digital signals with a ground, or a LOW, on pin 15.
Pin 8 is grounded since a single power source is used and
The clock frequency from IC2c and IC2b is applied to pin 14.

The output of the integrator, recovered information signal, is taken from pin 7 through R5.

The receiver circuit is contained on PC130-333 and consists of the components necessary to support the MC3418 CVSD demodulator chip.

The modulator chip is set up to operate using analog inputs with +12 volts, or a HIGH on pin 15.

The output of the integrator, pin 7, is coupled to the comparator, pin 2, through R12.
The analog input is applied to pin 1 of IC1, the modulator, through R1, level control, and C1, coupling capacitor.
The transmitter circuit is contained on PC130-332 and consists of the components necessary to support the MC3418 CVSD modulator chip.

LESSON MENU
Let's begin the lesson on DM CIRCUIT OPERATION............................
Once one system is learned, you will have no trouble learning and operating other systems.
Both, the DM modulator and demodulator circuits use the MC3418 continuously variable slope delta modulator/demodulator IC chip.
The receiving DM circuit (demodulator) changes the digital pulse back into the original analog signal.
DM circuits (modulator) change analog signals into digital and then transmit over wires, cables or fiberoptics.
The second part of the experiment will set up and analyze the DM demodulator or receiver circuit using the DM signal from the modulator.
The modulator or transmitter is first studied, analyzed and set up to produce a DM signal from an analog input signal.
To gain an understanding of a DM circuit, you will observe the operation of a typical continuous Variable Slope (CVSD) DM transmitter and receiver circuit.
